# Check inventory

*Generated by scripts/gen-checks-doc.mjs — do not edit by hand.* Run `npm run gen:checks` after adding, renaming or re-severitying a check;
`test/docs.test.mjs` fails while this file and the registry disagree.

**235 checks** — 38 in `pre-launch`, 176 in `launch-audit`, 21 in `post-launch`.

Severity is what a finding costs: `blocker` stops a launch, `high` is losing something today,
`medium` and `low` are worth fixing, `info` reports a state rather than a fault. Tier is what a
check needs in order to run: `repo` reads files on disk, `http` makes requests, `browser` needs
the optional Playwright tier, `human` is a question only a person can answer.

## pre-launch — the gate

Runs against the repository and its build output before a deploy. Any `fail` exits 1 and blocks the launch; no flag softens one.

### hygiene (7)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hygiene.clean-tree` | blocker | repo | Uncommitted changes in the working tree | a build made from files that are in no commit, so the deploy cannot be reproduced |
| `hygiene.env-tracked` | blocker | repo | An environment file is tracked by git | real credentials committed to history, where rotating them is the only remedy |
| `hygiene.lockfile` | blocker | repo | The lockfiles do not name one package manager | two lockfiles disagreeing about versions, so the host installs something nobody tested |
| `hygiene.nested-git` | blocker | repo | A nested git repository below the root | a directory whose contents the outer repository does not track and a deploy therefore cannot carry |
| `hygiene.node-version` | blocker | repo | The running Node does not satisfy engines.node | a local build on a Node the host will not use, which is how a build passes here and fails in CI |
| `hygiene.pushed` | blocker | repo | HEAD is not pushed to its upstream | a deploy from a commit that exists on one machine only, which nobody else can roll back to |
| `hygiene.secrets-committed` | blocker | repo | A secret-shaped string is committed | an API key, token or private key published in the repository |

### placeholders (6)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `placeholders.analytics-id` | blocker | repo | A placeholder analytics id | a measurement id nobody replaced, so the launch collects no data and nobody notices for a month |
| `placeholders.copy` | blocker | repo | Placeholder copy in the site | lorem ipsum, TODO markers and unreplaced template tokens shipping as page content |
| `placeholders.dev-host` | blocker | repo | A development or staging host in the build output | a localhost or preview-deploy url shipped to production, where it is a dead link or a duplicate-content copy |
| `placeholders.form-id` | blocker | repo | A placeholder form endpoint | a contact form posting to an example endpoint, so every enquiry is lost silently |
| `placeholders.required-env` | blocker | repo | A required environment variable is not set | a production build interpolating an undefined variable into the page as an empty string |
| `placeholders.source-maps` | low | repo | Source maps referenced from the build | original source published alongside the bundle, readable by anybody who opens devtools |

### build (2)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `build.dir-found` | blocker | repo | No usable build output directory | an output directory that is missing, or that holds no root index.html for a host to serve |
| `build.succeeds` | blocker | repo | The production build failed | a deploy attempted from a build that never completed |

### output (16)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `output.404-page` | blocker | repo | The 404 page is missing, duplicated or indexable | a missing custom 404, or one that is the homepage, or one search engines will index |
| `output.canonical` | blocker | repo | A canonical is missing, relative, off-host or not self-referencing | pages that tell search engines to credit somebody else, or nothing at all |
| `output.charset` | blocker | repo | A page declares no character encoding | mojibake in any text that is not plain ASCII, which usually means the apostrophes |
| `output.descriptions` | blocker | repo | A meta description is missing or duplicated | pages with no description, or a template sharing one, so search engines write their own |
| `output.favicon-set` | blocker | repo | The favicon set is incomplete | a browser tab, a bookmark or a phone home screen falling back to a blank page icon |
| `output.h1` | blocker | repo | A page has no h1, or more than one | a page with no first-level heading, or several competing for it |
| `output.index-html` | blocker | repo | No index.html at the root of the build | a build whose homepage is not where a host looks for it |
| `output.internal-refs` | blocker | repo | An internal reference resolves to no file | a link, image, stylesheet or font that 404s the moment the site is live |
| `output.lang` | blocker | repo | A page has no lang attribute | a document whose language screen readers and translators have to guess at |
| `output.llms-txt` | info | repo | llms.txt | an llms.txt that is absent, or present but not in the format the convention specifies |
| `output.noindex-utility-pages` | blocker | repo | A utility page is indexable | a thank-you or preview page ranking in search, which is how visitors land mid-funnel on an empty page |
| `output.og-image` | blocker | repo | The og:image is missing, not raster, or the wrong size | a social card that renders blank, cropped, or as a grey box on every network |
| `output.robots-txt` | blocker | repo | robots.txt is missing, blocking, or points at another host | a staging robots.txt shipped to production, which is how a launch gets deindexed on day one |
| `output.sitemap` | blocker | repo | The sitemap is missing, off-host, or lists pages the build does not have | a sitemap that sends crawlers to staging urls or to pages that were never built |
| `output.titles` | blocker | repo | A title is missing or duplicated | pages with no title, or a whole template sharing one, which is what a search result shows |
| `output.viewport` | blocker | repo | A page has no viewport meta | a page that renders at desktop width on a phone, zoomed out and unreadable |

### framework (4)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `framework.redirect-targets` | blocker | repo | A redirect destination resolves to nothing | a redirect rule that sends visitors and crawlers to a page the build does not contain |
| `framework.site-url` | blocker | repo | The configured site url is not the production url | a generator building absolute urls — canonicals, sitemap entries, social cards — for the wrong host |
| `framework.sitemap-integration` | blocker | repo | The sitemap integration produced no sitemap | a configured sitemap plugin that silently wrote nothing, so the build ships without one |
| `framework.trailing-slash` | blocker | repo | The trailing-slash policy contradicts the generated links | a config that says one thing and links that say another, so every internal link takes a redirect hop |

### predecessor (3)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `predecessor.coverage` | blocker | repo | Old urls have nowhere to land | pages from the site being replaced that will 404 after the cutover, taking their links and rankings with them |
| `predecessor.redirect-chains` | blocker | repo | A redirect chain or loop | a redirect that lands on another redirect, costing a hop and some authority, or a loop that serves nothing |
| `predecessor.wildcard-redirects` | blocker | repo | A wildcard redirect swallows old content urls | a catch-all rule that answers every old article with one page, which search engines read as a soft 404 |

## launch-audit — the auditor

Crawls a staging or live url and reports. It always exits 0 — it reports, it does not gate.

### inventory (7)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inventory.capped` | info | http | The audit stopped short of some urls | Every url the crawl refused, and every probe set that hit its cap — what this report does not cover. |
| `inventory.deep-page` | low | http | A page buried more than three clicks from the front page | A page the crawl only reached at depth four or deeper — a page nobody browsing the site is likely to find. |
| `inventory.non-200-page` | high | http | A page of this site answers with an error | A crawled url whose final response is a 4xx or a 5xx — a page that is linked or listed but does not load. |
| `inventory.orphan-page` | medium | http | A page the sitemap advertises that nothing on the site links to | A sitemap url no crawled page links to — reachable only by typing its address or finding it in search. |
| `inventory.target-unreachable` | blocker | http | The audit never read the url it was pointed at | A start url that was never fetched, one that never answered, or a crawl that parsed no HTML at all — an audit with no content under it. |
| `inventory.unlisted-page` | low | http | A page the site links to that the sitemap leaves out | A page the crawl reached by following links that no sitemap entry mentions. |
| `inventory.unreachable-page` | medium | http | A page of this site never answered at all | A crawled url whose request failed outright — DNS, TLS, a refused connection or a timeout — rather than returning a status. |

### indexability (25)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `indexability.ai-crawler-policy` | info | http | AI crawler policy | An AI crawler stance nobody chose on purpose. |
| `indexability.canonical-header-mismatch` | medium | http | The canonical header and tag disagree | A Link: rel=canonical header fighting the one in the markup. |
| `indexability.canonical-missing` | medium | http | A page declares no canonical url | Pages reachable at several urls with nothing saying which one counts. |
| `indexability.canonical-multiple` | high | http | A page declares more than one canonical | Two canonical tags, usually one from the theme and one from the SEO plugin. |
| `indexability.canonical-other-host` | high | http | A canonical points at another host | A canonical left pointing at the staging or pre-migration domain. |
| `indexability.canonical-relative` | medium | http | A canonical url is relative | A canonical written as a path, which resolves differently on www, apex and staging. |
| `indexability.canonical-to-redirect-or-404` | high | http | A canonical points at a redirect or a dead url | A canonical left behind by a url change. |
| `indexability.hreflang-invalid` | medium | http | A page declares an invalid hreflang code | en_US, english, or a region code in the wrong half of the pair. |
| `indexability.hreflang-no-x-default` | low | http | The hreflang cluster has no x-default | A multi-language site with nothing to serve a language it does not cover. |
| `indexability.hreflang-not-reciprocal` | medium | http | An hreflang alternate does not point back | A one-way hreflang cluster, which search engines discard entirely. |
| `indexability.llms-txt` | info | http | llms.txt | Whether the site offers an llms.txt, and whether it is shaped like one. |
| `indexability.nosnippet-unintended` | low | http | A page suppresses its search snippet | A nosnippet directive that silently strips the description from search results. |
| `indexability.page-noindex-in-sitemap` | high | http | A sitemap page is noindexed | A page advertised in the sitemap that its own markup tells Google to drop. |
| `indexability.robots-blocks-assets` | high | http | robots.txt blocks CSS or JavaScript | A disallow rule that stops Google rendering the page it is trying to rank. |
| `indexability.robots-sitemap-line-missing` | medium | http | robots.txt names no sitemap | A sitemap that exists but is never advertised where crawlers look first. |
| `indexability.robots-sitemap-other-host` | high | http | robots.txt points at a sitemap on another host | A sitemap url left pointing at the old domain or the staging host. |
| `indexability.robots-unfetchable` | high | http | robots.txt cannot be fetched | A robots.txt that errors, which some crawlers read as "stay out entirely". |
| `indexability.site-noindex` | blocker | http | The site tells search engines not to index it | A staging noindex left behind on the production launch. |
| `indexability.sitemap-invalid` | high | http | The sitemap did not fully parse | A sitemap index whose child is missing, unreachable, or not XML. |
| `indexability.sitemap-lastmod-future` | low | http | A sitemap lastmod is in the future | A generator stamping lastmod from a clock nobody set. |
| `indexability.sitemap-missing` | high | http | No sitemap could be found | A launch with no sitemap at any conventional path and none named in robots.txt. |
| `indexability.sitemap-noindexed-url` | high | http | A sitemap url is kept out of the index | A sitemap url blocked by robots.txt or by an X-Robots-Tag header. |
| `indexability.sitemap-other-host` | high | http | The sitemap lists urls on another host | A sitemap generated against the staging or pre-migration domain. |
| `indexability.sitemap-too-large` | medium | http | The sitemap exceeds 50,000 urls | A single sitemap file past the limit crawlers will read. |
| `indexability.sitemap-url-not-200` | high | http | A sitemap url does not return 200 | A sitemap still advertising pages that have been deleted or moved. |

### host (24)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `host.404-no-navigation` | low | http | The 404 page offers no way back | A dead end: an error page with no navigation and nowhere to click. |
| `host.cert-expiring` | high | http | The TLS certificate expires soon | A certificate with days left and no renewal in sight. |
| `host.cert-invalid` | blocker | http | The TLS certificate does not validate | A self-signed, expired, or wrong-host certificate: a full-page browser warning. |
| `host.cert-missing-san` | high | http | The certificate does not cover both apex and www | A certificate issued for one host variant while the other is still reachable. |
| `host.default-404-body` | medium | http | The 404 page is the server default | A stock nginx, Apache or framework error page on a finished site. |
| `host.dev-host-leak` | blocker | http | A page references a development host | localhost, a tunnel url, or the old staging host, shipped to production. |
| `host.hsts-missing` | medium | http | No Strict-Transport-Security header | An https site that still lets the first request go out in the clear. |
| `host.hsts-short` | low | http | The HSTS max-age is under a year | A max-age too short for preload lists and long-lived browser state. |
| `host.http-not-redirected` | high | http | http:// is served instead of redirecting to https:// | A site still answering on plain http after the certificate went up. |
| `host.http-redirect-not-301` | medium | http | The http to https redirect is temporary | A 302 where the permanent move deserves a 301. |
| `host.http-version` | info | http | HTTP version | Whether the origin advertises a protocol newer than HTTP/1.1. |
| `host.leaky-header-present` | low | http | A response header discloses the stack | Server, X-Powered-By and friends, naming the software and version to attack. |
| `host.meta-refresh` | medium | http | A page redirects with a meta refresh | A client-side refresh standing in for a server redirect. |
| `host.mixed-content` | high | http | An https page loads http subresources | A hardcoded http:// asset that browsers block or flag on a secure page. |
| `host.no-cache-static` | low | http | A static asset is served without caching | Fingerprinted assets re-downloaded on every visit. |
| `host.no-compression` | medium | http | HTML is served uncompressed | A server that never negotiated gzip or brotli. |
| `host.redirect-chain` | medium | http | A url redirects more than once | Stacked redirects — http to https to www to path — costing a round trip each. |
| `host.redirect-loop` | high | http | A url redirects in a loop | A redirect rule that sends a url back to itself, so the page never loads. |
| `host.security-header-coop-corp` | info | http | The cross-origin isolation headers are not set | COOP/CORP left off — worth knowing, not worth blocking a launch over. |
| `host.security-header-missing` | medium | http | A recommended security header is missing | A response with none of the headers the OWASP Secure Headers project asks for. |
| `host.soft-404` | high | http | A missing page answers 200 | A catch-all route turning every typo into an indexable empty page. |
| `host.trailing-slash-both-200` | medium | http | Both trailing-slash forms serve 200 | One page reachable at /path and /path/, with no redirect between them. |
| `host.www-apex-no-redirect` | medium | http | The other host variant does not redirect here | A www (or apex) host that errors instead of redirecting to the canonical one. |
| `host.www-apex-split` | high | http | Both www and apex serve the site | Two hosts serving one site, splitting links and rankings between them. |

### head (35)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `head.apple-touch-icon-missing` | low | http | No apple-touch-icon is declared | A site saved to an iOS home screen as a screenshot of the page instead of an icon. |
| `head.charset-missing` | low | http | The page declares no character encoding | A document with no charset, where anything but ASCII renders as mojibake. |
| `head.description-duplicate` | medium | http | Several pages share one description | One description copied across pages, usually the site tagline. |
| `head.description-length` | low | http | A description is too short or too long | A description under fifty characters or past the hundred and sixty a snippet shows. |
| `head.description-missing` | medium | http | A page has no meta description | A page with no description, leaving the search snippet to whatever text the crawler picks. |
| `head.duplicate-id` | low | http | A page repeats an element id | The same id on two elements, which breaks label targets, anchors and every querySelector. |
| `head.favicon-broken` | medium | http | A declared icon does not load | An icon link pointing at a url that 404s, usually after a path change. |
| `head.favicon-missing` | medium | http | The page links no favicon | A site with no icon, which every tab, bookmark and history entry shows blank. |
| `head.h1-missing` | medium | http | A page has no h1 | A page whose main heading was styled as a div, leaving nothing to announce it. |
| `head.h1-multiple` | low | http | A page has more than one h1 | A template where both the site name and the page heading are h1. |
| `head.heading-empty` | low | http | A heading has no text | An empty heading left behind as a spacer or by a CMS field nobody filled in. |
| `head.heading-skip` | low | http | A heading level is skipped | An h1 followed by an h3, where the level was chosen for its font size. |
| `head.jsonld-invalid` | high | http | A JSON-LD block does not parse | Structured data with a trailing comma or an unescaped quote, which is discarded whole. |
| `head.jsonld-missing-required` | medium | http | Structured data is missing a required property | A schema.org node that parses but cannot produce the rich result it was written for. |
| `head.jsonld-on-noindex` | low | http | Structured data sits on a noindexed page | Markup written for a rich result on a page no search engine will index. |
| `head.jsonld-types-summary` | info | http | Structured data types found | Nothing: this is the inventory of what the site actually declares, grouped by template. |
| `head.jsonld-url-broken` | medium | http | Structured data points at a url that does not load | A url, logo or image in JSON-LD that the crawl already found broken. |
| `head.lang-missing` | medium | http | The html element declares no language | A document with no lang attribute, which a screen reader has to guess a voice for. |
| `head.manifest-missing` | info | http | No web app manifest is linked | A site with no manifest, which cannot be installed and names itself by its title alone. |
| `head.meta-duplicate` | low | http | A meta tag is declared twice | Two descriptions, or two canonical-ish og tags, where only the first is used. |
| `head.meta-outside-head` | medium | http | A meta tag sits outside the head | A description or og tag injected into the body, where nothing reads it. |
| `head.og-image-broken` | high | http | The og:image does not load | A card image url that 404s, which turns every shared link into a text-only preview. |
| `head.og-image-dimensions-missing` | low | http | The og:image declares no dimensions | A card with no og:image:width/height, so the first share renders before the image is measured. |
| `head.og-image-not-raster` | medium | http | The og:image is not a raster image | An SVG — or something that is not an image at all — used as a social card. |
| `head.og-image-small` | medium | http | The og:image is smaller than a card needs | A card image under 1200×630, which social networks upscale or crop to a thumbnail. |
| `head.og-missing` | medium | http | An Open Graph property is missing | A page that produces a bare, untitled link preview when it is shared. |
| `head.og-url-mismatch` | medium | http | og:url and the canonical disagree | Two different urls claimed for one page, which splits shares and likes between them. |
| `head.theme-color-missing` | info | http | No theme colour is declared | A site whose browser chrome stays default grey on mobile. |
| `head.title-duplicate` | high | http | Several pages share one title | A template that writes the same <title> onto every page it renders. |
| `head.title-framework-default` | high | http | A title is still the framework default | A starter-template title ("Astro", "Create Next App", "Document") that shipped to production. |
| `head.title-length` | low | http | A title is too short or too long | A title under ten characters or past the sixty a search result shows. |
| `head.title-missing` | high | http | A page has no title | A page shipped without a <title>, which search results and browser tabs fall back to the url for. |
| `head.twitter-card-missing` | low | http | No twitter:card is declared | A page that has no card format chosen, so a shared link renders as plain text or a small thumbnail. |
| `head.viewport-blocks-zoom` | medium | http | The viewport stops the page being zoomed | user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1, which takes pinch-zoom away from everyone. |
| `head.viewport-missing` | high | http | The page declares no viewport | A page with no viewport meta, which a phone renders at desktop width and shrinks. |

### links (15)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `links.empty-anchor` | low | http | A link has no text and no accessible name | An icon or wrapper link with no text, no image alt and no aria-label — unreadable to a screen reader. |
| `links.external-broken` | medium | http | A link points at a page on another site that is not there | An outbound link whose target answers 404, 410 or a server error. |
| `links.external-unverifiable` | info | http | An outbound link could not be checked | An external target that timed out, refused an anonymous request, or rate-limited the audit — checked by hand, not by this tool. |
| `links.generic-anchor-text` | info | http | A link is labelled "click here" | Anchor text that describes clicking rather than the destination. |
| `links.hash-href` | low | http | A link points at nothing but "#" | href="#", a placeholder that jumps to the top of the page instead of going anywhere. |
| `links.internal-broken` | high | http | A link points at a page of this site that is not there | A same-origin link to a url that answers 404 or 500 — a renamed page, a typo, a deleted draft. |
| `links.javascript-href` | medium | http | A link runs script instead of going somewhere | href="javascript:…", which is dead without JavaScript and is not a link to anything. |
| `links.mailto-invalid` | medium | http | A mailto: link has no usable address | mailto: with an empty or malformed address — a contact link that opens an empty mail window. |
| `links.noopener-missing` | low | http | A new-tab link has no rel="noopener" | target="_blank" without noopener, which hands the opened page a handle back to this one. |
| `links.same-text-different-target` | info | http | One link label is used for two different destinations | Two links reading the same thing and going to different places, which a screen-reader link list cannot tell apart. |
| `links.skip-link-missing` | low | http | Pages have no skip link | No "skip to content" link, so a keyboard user tabs through the whole navigation on every page. |
| `links.tel-invalid` | medium | http | A tel: link is not a phone number | tel: carrying words or too few digits, so tapping it on a phone dials nothing. |
| `links.to-dev-host` | blocker | http | A link points at a development host | localhost, a preview deployment or the staging host, linked from a page that shipped. |
| `links.to-http-on-https` | medium | http | An https page links to a plain-http url | A link left on http from a page served over https — a downgrade, and often a redirect or a dead host. |
| `links.to-redirecting-internal` | low | http | An internal link goes through a redirect | A same-origin link written to the old url, so every visit costs an extra round trip. |

### images (10)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `images.alt-missing` | high | http | An image has no alt attribute | An <img> with no alt at all, which a screen reader announces by reading out the file name. |
| `images.broken` | high | http | An image does not load | An <img src> that answers 404 or an error — a hole in the page where a picture should be. |
| `images.dimensions-missing` | medium | http | An image declares no width or height | An <img> with neither attribute, so the page reflows when it loads. |
| `images.duplicate-across-pages` | low | http | The same image file is served under two urls | One picture uploaded twice under different names, so no visitor ever gets it from cache. |
| `images.lazy-on-first-image` | medium | http | The first image on the page is lazy-loaded | loading="lazy" on the hero image, which delays the one picture the visitor is waiting for. |
| `images.legacy-format` | low | http | An image is served only as JPEG or PNG | A bare .jpg or .png with no <picture> and no srcset, so no browser can take a smaller modern format. |
| `images.not-lazy-below-fold` | low | http | Images below the fold load eagerly | Images past the third with no loading="lazy", downloaded before anyone scrolls to them. |
| `images.oversized` | medium | http | An image is larger than half a megabyte | A photo shipped straight from the camera, or an uncompressed export. |
| `images.video-autoplay-sound` | medium | http | A video autoplays with sound | <video autoplay> without muted — a browser blocks it, and where it does not, it is the worst first impression a site can make. |
| `images.video-captions-missing` | info | http | A video has no captions | A <video> with no <track>, which is unusable to anyone who cannot hear it or is not using sound. |

### forms (8)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `forms.dead-action` | high | http | A form posts nowhere | A form with no action, an action of "#", or a javascript: action — every submission is lost. |
| `forms.dev-endpoint` | blocker | http | A form posts to a development host | A form action still pointing at localhost, a preview deployment or the staging host. |
| `forms.embed-broken` | high | http | A form embed does not load | An embedded form or booking widget whose script or iframe answers 404 — the form simply never appears. |
| `forms.inventory` | info | http | A form on the site | Nothing — this is the list of every form the audit found, so none of them is forgotten. |
| `forms.no-spam-protection` | info | http | A form has no spam protection | A public form with neither a honeypot nor a captcha, which bots will find within days of launch. |
| `forms.placeholder-id` | high | http | A form still carries a placeholder id | A form endpoint or hidden field left as "your-form-id", "xxxx" or an example property id. |
| `forms.test-submission-required` | info | human | Submit this form yourself before launch | The one thing no HTTP request can prove: that a submitted form reaches a mailbox somebody reads. |
| `forms.unlabelled-inputs` | medium | http | A form control has no label | A field with no <label>, aria-label or aria-labelledby — unlabelled to a screen reader, and often to everyone once the placeholder disappears. |

### a11y (9)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a11y.autofocus` | low | http | A page takes focus away on load | An autofocus attribute, which moves the cursor before the visitor has read anything. |
| `a11y.browser-tier-required` | info | http | The accessibility audit is only as deep as HTML goes | The gap this tier cannot cover: colour contrast, focus order as rendered, keyboard traps and everything axe would have found in a real browser. |
| `a11y.form-labels` | high | http | A form control has no accessible name | An input, select or textarea with no <label>, aria-label or aria-labelledby — a field a screen reader announces as nothing at all. |
| `a11y.heading-order` | low | http | A page skips a heading level | A heading that jumps more than one level below the heading before it — an h1 followed by an h3, say. |
| `a11y.iframe-title-missing` | medium | http | An embedded frame has no title | An <iframe> with no title attribute — a map, a video or a form a screen reader can only announce as "frame". |
| `a11y.image-alt-coverage` | info | http | How much of this site is described for screen readers | The share of images across the crawled pages that carry an alt attribute at all. |
| `a11y.link-text-empty` | medium | http | A link announces nothing at all | An anchor with no text, no image alt and no aria-label — a link a screen reader can only read out as its url. |
| `a11y.main-landmark-missing` | medium | http | Pages with no main region | A page with no <main> and no role="main" — nothing for "skip to content" to skip to. |
| `a11y.tabindex-positive` | low | http | A page overrides the tab order with a positive tabindex | tabindex="1" or higher, which pulls an element out of the document order and in front of everything else. |

### perf (7)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `perf.browser-tier-required` | info | http | Nothing here is a measurement | The gap this tier cannot cover: the page was never rendered, so no Core Web Vital was measured. |
| `perf.font-display-missing` | low | http | A web font has no font-display, so text waits for it | An @font-face block that fetches a font file and declares no font-display — by default the browser hides the text for up to three seconds while it loads. |
| `perf.hero-preload-missing` | info | http | Nothing tells the browser which image matters most | A page whose first <img> is neither preloaded nor marked fetchpriority="high" — the browser finds it only after parsing. |
| `perf.page-weight` | medium | http | A page weighs more than three megabytes | A page whose HTML plus the assets the audit could size already exceeds 3 MB — before anything it could not size. |
| `perf.render-blocking-script` | medium | http | The head waits for a script before showing anything | A <script src> in the head with no defer, no async, no nomodule and no type="module" — the browser stops parsing until it has fetched and run it. |
| `perf.request-count` | low | http | A page asks the browser for more than a hundred things | More than 100 referenced images, scripts, stylesheets and frames on a single page. |
| `perf.third-party-scripts` | info | http | Code this site loads from somebody else | Every script served from a host that is not this site, grouped by host — each one a connection, a dependency and a privacy question. |

### analytics (5)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `analytics.duplicate-install` | medium | http | A page installs the same analytics tool twice | A tag in both the layout and a page template, which doubles pageviews and halves the bounce rate. |
| `analytics.inconsistent-ids` | high | http | Pages report to different analytics properties | Two measurement ids across one site — usually an old property left in a template after a rebuild. |
| `analytics.missing-on-pages` | medium | http | The analytics tag is missing from some pages | A tag in the main layout but not in a landing page or checkout template, so those visits are never counted. |
| `analytics.none-detected` | high | http | No analytics tag anywhere on the site | A launch with no measurement at all: no baseline, and no way to tell afterwards whether it worked. |
| `analytics.summary` | info | http | The analytics tools installed on this site | Nothing — this is the list of what is measuring the site, so an unexpected entry is visible. |

### content (8)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `content.address-variants` | info | http | The site publishes more than one postal address | A second address left behind after a move — which search engines read as two businesses. |
| `content.broken-entity` | low | http | An HTML entity is visible in the text | Text escaped twice, so the reader sees "&amp;" or "&nbsp;" where a character should be. |
| `content.copyright-year-stale` | low | http | The copyright year is out of date | A footer year hardcoded at build time and never updated — the cheapest signal that a site is abandoned. |
| `content.email-variants` | info | http | The site publishes more than one email address | Several contact addresses across the site, at least one of which nobody monitors. |
| `content.mixed-spelling` | info | http | The site uses two spellings of the same word | American and British spellings of one word across the site — two writers who never agreed. |
| `content.past-dated-promo` | medium | http | A promotion advertises a date that has passed | "Ends Aug 31" still on the page in September — an offer the site is still making and can no longer honour. |
| `content.phone-variants` | medium | http | The site publishes more than one phone number | An old number left on one page and the new one on another, so half the calls go nowhere. |
| `content.placeholder-text` | high | http | A page still carries placeholder copy | Lorem ipsum, "coming soon", a TODO, an unrendered {{ template }} or an [INSERT] left in the copy. |

### redirects (8)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redirects.chain` | medium | http | An old url takes more than one hop to arrive | A redirect chain — two or more hops — which costs a round trip each and which some crawlers stop following. |
| `redirects.new-site-error` | high | http | An old url hits an error on the new site that is not a missing page | An old url the new origin answers with a 500, a 403 or anything else that is neither a success nor a 404 — broken or locked down, not gone. |
| `redirects.old-url-required` | info | http | No old site was given, so no old url was checked | A launch-audit run with no --old-url: if this site replaces an existing one, nothing here says whether its urls survived. |
| `redirects.old-url-same-origin` | info | http | The old url given is the same site being audited | An --old-url on the origin under audit, which cannot produce a redirect map: every path would trivially match itself. |
| `redirects.summary` | info | http | What the new site does with every old url | The count of old urls by outcome, and the pointer to the full map in redirects.csv. |
| `redirects.to-404` | high | http | A redirect sends an old url to an error page | An old url that does redirect — and lands on a 404 or a 410. Worse than no redirect, because the server looks like it handled it. |
| `redirects.wildcard-smell` | medium | http | A catch-all rule is standing in for a redirect map | More than 30% of the old urls landing on one page — the signature of a wildcard rule that redirects everything to the front page. |
| `redirects.would-404` | high | http | An old url has nothing waiting for it on the new site | A url the old site served that the new site answers with a 404 or a 410 and does not redirect — every link and bookmark to it is now dead. |

### ops (3)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ops.checklist` | info | human | Launch readiness: the jobs that are not in the markup | The thirteen ops and access items every launch needs, each marked with the check that verifies it or as somebody's job. |
| `ops.email-auth` | medium | http | Mail from this domain is not authenticated | A missing SPF, DKIM or DMARC record — the three things that decide whether a form notification reaches an inbox or a spam folder. |
| `ops.legal-pages` | medium | http | Nothing on this site links to a privacy policy, terms or a cookie policy | No link anywhere on the crawled site whose text or href mentions privacy, terms or cookies. |

### browser (12)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `browser.analytics-not-firing` | high | browser | The analytics tag is installed but never sends anything | A measurement snippet that is in the markup and does not fire — a blocked script, a consent gate that never resolves, a misconfigured id — which markup alone can never reveal. |
| `browser.axe-violation` | medium | browser | axe found an accessibility violation | Everything the html tier structurally cannot check: colour contrast, computed roles and names, focus handling, ARIA state as rendered. |
| `browser.consent-missing` | info | browser | Cookies are set before anyone is asked | Analytics cookies written on load with no consent banner in sight — the shape of a GDPR/ePrivacy problem, which is a lawyer question rather than a bug. |
| `browser.console-errors` | medium | browser | The page logs javascript errors in the console | Scripts that throw on load — a broken widget, a missing global, a failed integration — which the html tier cannot see because the markup is fine. |
| `browser.embed-console-error` | high | browser | An embedded form or widget is throwing errors | A third-party form, booking widget or payment embed that loads but does not work — the failure mode that silently loses every enquiry a site receives. |
| `browser.failed-requests` | medium | browser | The page asks for files that do not load | Broken images, stylesheets and scripts as the browser actually requests them, including the ones built by script that never appear in the markup. |
| `browser.horizontal-overflow` | medium | browser | The page scrolls sideways | A too-wide element — an image, a table, a fixed-width block — that makes the whole page scroll horizontally. On a phone it is the single most common visible layout bug. |
| `browser.lighthouse-score` | medium | browser | The Lighthouse performance score is below the bar | A page that is slow as measured rather than as guessed — the number the http tier can only approximate from asset weight. |
| `browser.lighthouse-summary` | info | browser | Lighthouse scores for this page | Nothing on its own — it is the measured baseline the other findings are argued against, recorded so the next run has something to compare with. |
| `browser.nav-not-collapsed` | medium | browser | The mobile navigation does not collapse | A menu with a burger button whose links are still on screen at phone width — the state a half-finished responsive nav ships in. |
| `browser.rendered-head-differs` | medium | browser | The head a browser sees is not the head that was served | A title, description, canonical or robots meta that javascript rewrites after load — so what a crawler that runs scripts indexes is not what the server sent. |
| `browser.screenshots-for-review` | info | browser | Screenshots captured for a human visual pass | Nothing automatically — it hands over the evidence for the one review no checker can do: does this page actually look right. |

## post-launch — the watch

Runs the moment DNS has moved and once a day for thirty days after. It always exits 0.

### cutover (21)

| id | severity | tier | title | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cutover.analytics-missing` | high | http | An analytics tag that was there before is missing now | A measurement tag lost in the cutover — the launch runs unmeasured, and the gap in the data is permanent. |
| `cutover.analytics-not-firing` | high | browser | The analytics tag is installed and never sends a hit | A tag present in the markup whose collector is never called when the page actually renders — consent gating, a blocked script, a bad id. |
| `cutover.baseline-changed` | medium | http | A page changed between the baseline and production | A title, description, canonical, robots directive, h1 or schema type that is not what it was before the launch. |
| `cutover.baseline-missing-page` | high | http | A page the baseline recorded is no longer served | A page that existed before the launch and that a crawl of production can no longer reach. |
| `cutover.baseline-new-redirect` | medium | http | A page that used to be served directly now redirects | A url in the baseline that answered on its own and now takes a hop — a url that other pages and search results still point at. |
| `cutover.canonical-host` | high | http | www and apex are not one canonical host | Both host variants serving the site after the cutover, or the other variant failing instead of redirecting. |
| `cutover.dns-propagation` | info | http | What each public resolver currently answers | The propagation picture: the same question asked of Google, Cloudflare, Quad9 and OpenDNS, and whether their answers agree yet. |
| `cutover.dns-unexpected` | high | http | A resolver answers with something other than the expected target | DNS that has not moved, or has moved to the wrong record, seen from a public resolver rather than from this machine. |
| `cutover.form-endpoint-down` | high | http | A form endpoint does not answer | A form action or a third-party form embed that stopped resolving at the cutover — the site looks fine and every submission is lost. |
| `cutover.http-redirect` | high | http | http:// does not permanently redirect to https:// | A plain-http origin still serving the site, or redirecting temporarily, after the cutover. |
| `cutover.https-cert-host` | blocker | http | The certificate served does not cover the live host | A certificate that did not validate, or that was issued before the host moved and never covered it — every visitor gets an interstitial warning. |
| `cutover.human-items` | info | human | The six things on cutover day that no script can do | The human half of the day: submissions, verification and the announcement, in the order they depend on each other. |
| `cutover.noindex-live` | blocker | http | Production still tells search engines not to index it | The staging noindex — meta, X-Robots-Tag or a blanket robots.txt Disallow — shipped to the live host. |
| `cutover.old-host-serving-content` | high | http | The old host is still serving its own site | An old domain that answers with its own pages after the cutover instead of redirecting to the new one. |
| `cutover.redirect-drift` | high | http | A redirect no longer does what the redirect map says | A row of redirects.csv that answers a temporary redirect, takes more than one hop, lands somewhere else, or is still missing. |
| `cutover.redirect-unverified` | medium | http | A redirect row could not be checked at all | An old url that answered nothing when it was re-requested — a DNS failure, a timeout, a refused connection. Unknown, not broken. |
| `cutover.robots-live` | high | http | robots.txt on the live host is missing or points somewhere else | A robots.txt the production host does not serve, or one still naming the staging host. |
| `cutover.security-headers-regressed` | medium | http | A security header the baseline had is gone | A response header that was present before the launch and is absent on production — usually a platform default that the new host does not share. |
| `cutover.sitemap-live` | high | http | No sitemap answers on the live host | A sitemap that did not survive the cutover: none discoverable, or the one robots.txt names not answering 200. |
| `cutover.sitemap-references-staging` | high | http | The live sitemap or robots.txt advertises a non-production host | Sitemap <loc> entries, or a robots.txt Sitemap: line, still pointing at staging after the cutover — an invitation to index the wrong copy. |
| `cutover.staging-still-indexable` | high | http | The staging copy is still live and still indexable | A staging host that answers 200 with no noindex and no redirect — a full duplicate of the new site, competing with it. |
